strategy_title: Reindex xindex decomposition to eliminate stride-2 warp loads
strategy_description: When the innermost warp dimension (xindex % N) maps to a stride-2 position in a global tensor, consecutive threads access elements 8 bytes apart, causing every warp to touch 2 cache lines instead of 1 and generating ~50% excessive sectors (flagged by UncoalescedGlobalAccess). Fixing this by reducing XBLOCK so the innermost decomposition variable maps to the stride-1 dimension of the tensor (e.g., changing x0 = xindex%32 with offset 2*x0 to x0 = xindex%64 with offset x0) eliminates the stride-2 pattern, cuts DRAM throughput from 82% to 11%, raises L1 hit rate from 27% to 68%, and reduces warp stall cycles by ~44%. Switching eviction policy from evict_last to evict_first on streaming loads that are not reused across CTAs further prevents L1 cache pollution.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=128, stride-2 uncoalesced
x0 = xindex % 32          # maps to stride-2 dim -> UNCOALESCED
x1 = (xindex // 32) % 32
x2 = (xindex // 1024) % 16
x3 = xindex // 16384
# Load offset has factor 2*x0 -> stride-2
tmp = tl.load(ptr + (2*x0 + 128*x1 + 8192*x2 + 131072*r + 2097152*x3),
              eviction_policy='evict_last')
fast_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=64, stride-1 coalesced
x0 = xindex % 64          # maps to stride-1 dim -> COALESCED
x1 = (xindex // 64) % 32
x2 = (xindex // 2048) % 16
x3 = xindex // 32768
# Load offset has factor x0 (no multiplier) -> stride-1
tmp = tl.load(ptr + (x0 + 64*x1 + 4096*x2 + 131072*r + 2097152*x3),
              eviction_policy='evict_first')
# Also add @triton.autotune with XBLOCK in [32,64,128], num_warps in [4,8]
applicable_when: NCU UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule fires with >40% excessive sectors; DRAM throughput >70%; L1 hit rate <35%; warp stall cycles dominated by L1TEX dependency (CPIStall_L1TEX >60%); the load index contains a factor of 2 (or other integer >1) applied to the variable derived from xindex%N, indicating the innermost warp dimension maps to a non-unit stride in the tensor layout.
do_not_apply_when: The tensor's innermost dimension is already stride-1 and the load index has no multiplier on the warp-lane variable; when DRAM throughput is low and the bottleneck is compute or shared memory; when reducing XBLOCK would break the correctness of the index decomposition for other tensors accessed in the same kernel.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: XBLOCK controls how many x-dimension elements each program handles. Changing XBLOCK from 128 to 64 here was necessary to make xindex%64 align with the 64-element stride-1 last dimension of the tensor. Adding @triton.autotune allows the runtime to select the best XBLOCK. The evict_first policy in Triton is equivalent to CUDA's __ldcs (streaming cache hint) — use it for data that is read once and not reused across thread blocks.
